saints.name: St. Cyril of Alexandria
saints.title: Bishop and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The patriarch who championed the title “Mother of God” and led the Council of Ephesus against Nestorius…
biography: Born about 376, Cyril was nephew to Theophilus, patriarch of Alexandria, whom he accompanied to the Synod of the Oak in 403 and succeeded in October 412. His first years were stormy: he shut the churches of the Novatianists, banished the Jews of Alexandria, and feuded with the prefect Orestes, and in 415 a Christian mob murdered the philosopher Hypatia; how far he was answerable is disputed still.

His lasting work began in 428, when Nestorius of Constantinople attacked the Virgin's title Theotokos, 'God-bearer.' For Cyril the word guarded the whole mystery: one and the same person, God the Son, was born of her and hung upon the cross. His letters and twelve anathemas rallied the Church, and presiding at the Council of Ephesus in 431 he won Nestorius's deposition, though briefly imprisoned by Theodosius II.

Reconciled with John of Antioch in 433, he ruled in peace until his death in 444, leaving commentaries and festal letters that made him the Church's great doctor of the Incarnation. He has been called the Pillar of Faith and the Seal of the Fathers, and Pope Leo XIII numbered him among the Doctors of the Church.
saints.knownFor: Defending the title “Mother of God” at Ephesus.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; Doctor of the Church (1883)
